Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
327 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Guidance have trended a little faster lifting the system
offshore of the Southeast U.S. coast Sunday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Coastal low pressure to bring light to moderate rain 
  Sunday.

- 2) Conditions turn cooler next week, with a coastal low 
     forecast to track up the East Coast later in the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Coastal low pressure to bring light to moderate rain
Sunday.

The low pressure center offshore of the Southeast U.S. coast is
expected to track a little quicker now on Sunday, while
remaining just offshore of the mid Atlantic coast. While rain is
expected everywhere in our CWA Sunday, amounts seem to have 
trended lower with areas east of I-95 expected to receive half 
inch of rain with any inch or greater totals remaining east of 
the Chesapeake Bay. The rain may persist into Sunday evening 
across southern MD before exiting the area by midnight Sunday 
night. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Conditions turn cooler next week, with a 
coastal low forecast to track up the East Coast later in the 
week.

Sunday's system will depart off toward the northeast on Monday. 
Winds will shift to out of the northwest, but cold advection will be 
minimal with the primary trough axis still off to our northwest over 
the Great Lakes. Temperatures are forecast to climb into the 60s to 
near 70 beneath a mix of sun and clouds.

A stronger surge of cold advection will move through Monday night. 
Cooler conditions are expected on Tuesday as a result, with highs 
forecast to be in the upper 40s to mid 50s (upper 30s to mid 40s 
mountains). Conditions will remain dry and winds will shift to out 
of the north as high pressure builds over the Great Lakes. 

High pressure will progress eastward toward New England on 
Wednesday. Meanwhile, a fast moving upper trough will translate 
eastward from the center of the CONUS toward the Appalachians. An 
area of low pressure will likely develop downstream of this trough 
along the Southeast US coast on Wednesday. This system will then 
track northward along the East Coast Wednesday night into Thursday. 
This far out, both deterministic and ensemble guidance show a wide 
range of potential solutions, so it's far too early to get into 
specific details. However, at least some precipitation appears 
likely. Current ensemble guidance suggests that precipitation would 
most likely fall as rain at lower elevations, with greater chances 
for wintry precipitation at higher elevations, especially across 
western portions of the forecast area. 

&&

.AVIATION /20Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Rain is expected to begin late Saturday night into Sunday
morning with MVFR conditions developing Sunday morning. Winds
are expected to remain below 10 kt under stable conditions. 

VFR conditions are expected on both Monday and Tuesday. Winds will 
be out of the northwest on Monday, before shifting to out of the 
north on Tuesday.

&&

.MARINE...

Winds will begin strengthening Saturday night into Sunday with
SCA conditions likely. 

Small Craft Advisory conditions appear possible over the waters at 
times in northwesterly flow on Monday, and then again in northerly 
flow Monday night into Tuesday.
